qs.q:
Extreme Sports — Which person…

A=Adam (rock climbing — ignored as child, solo climbing)
B=Benjamin (bungee jumping — waited until 18, once and never again)
C=Connor (BMX — grandpa helped, won cup)
D=Daniel (skating half-pipes — friends excluded him)
E=Ethan (surfing — injured, watching TV until recovery)
F=Finley (mountain bike spectator — brother does downhill racing)

0. likes fighting gravity? [E=Ethan: 'catching and riding waves']
1. was quick to make progress?
2. couldn't cope with the adrenaline rush?
3. was afraid at the beginning?
4. was too frightened to try the sport?
5. did not have his parents' permission?
6. felt ignored by his friends?
7. could not afford the equipment?
8. enjoys watching the sport?
9. won a competition?
10. enjoys the danger?
11. wishes he had done the sport?
12. has to take a break from the sport?
items: 2 — couldn't cope with the adrenaline rush?
4 — was too frightened to try the sport?
5 — did not have his parents' permission?
11 — wishes he had done the sport?
12 — has to take a break from the sport?

qs.q:
Going Underground

"Although I passed my driving test, living and working in a crowded city of ten million people, I could never see the point in owning a car. I suppose it's just that I've got used to it after all this time."

Why does the author use the underground railway?
A It's cheaper than other means of transport.
B It allows her to escape the bad weather.
C It's something she does out of habit.
D She has never learnt how to drive.
opts: It's cheaper than other means of transport.
It allows her to escape the bad weather.
It's something she does out of habit.
She has never learnt how to drive.

qs.q:
Going Underground

"I notice that, unlike me, many passengers use their daily trips as an opportunity to catch up with their unfinished business. There are always commuters with their laptops or going over reports. Some simply like to watch the capital's inhabitants... I'm definitely one of the former."

The author likes to spend her time on the underground…
A getting some work done.
B observing other people.
C reading a good book.
D having a short nap.

Going Underground

"I'm convinced that the majority of commuters would consider the consumption of snacks such as burgers to be the most anti-social practice on our journeys. Loud music on iPods or phones, especially rap and heavy metal, probably wouldn't be far behind."

Which behaviour does the author dislike most on the underground?
A Reading newspapers.
B Playing music.
C Kissing.
D Eating.

Going Underground

"A proud-looking old man getting upset when a young woman got up and vacated her seat for him. 'Young lady. Do you think I'm too weak to stand on my own two feet?' he roared. She was only trying to help. The poor girl was horrified."

Why did the author tell the little story in the fifth paragraph?
A To show that you should be careful not to offend people.
B To show that funny things happen on the underground.
C To show that people can be rude on public transport.
D To show that old people can be very independent.
opts: To show that you should be careful not to offend people.
To show that funny things happen on the underground.
To show that people can be rude on public transport.
To show that old people can be very independent.

qs.q:
Going Underground

"They are a distinguishing characteristic of our transport system. It'd be a shame if busking was made illegal."

What's the author's opinion of the musicians who play in underground stations?
A They are a special feature of the underground system.
B They create a negative impression of the city.
C There should be a law passed against them.
D They are not as good as they used to be.
opts: They are a special feature of the underground system.
They create a negative impression of the city.
There should be a law passed against them.
They are not as good as they used to be.

qs.q:
Going Underground — What was the author's aim in writing the article?
A To propose improvements to the underground.
B To offer a personal view of the underground.
C To give advice on using the underground.
D To criticise the underground system.
opts: To propose improvements to the underground.
To offer a personal view of the underground.
To give advice on using the underground.

B However, we also have another aim, and that's raising money for charity.
C In fact, drinking enough liquid will be one of the greatest difficulties.

F If we're in serious trouble, then we can obviously get help.
G But that's not the only physical danger you're exposed to.
H The problem is how we are going to carry it all.
